audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart rows 4-5 and 6 read 'Skill' in both layers while the packet chart gives Irelia, and the whys for those rows describe clear Irelia advantages (staying glued through the root, Vanguard's Edge pinning him mid-drain). Row 7 (2+ items) reads 'Irelia' while whys[6] and late both say a scaled Swain wins the 5v5.
audit.why: 53.54% winrate over 508 games with a text body that describes Irelia owning levels 4-6 and Swain owning the late game. Chart contradicted its own prose.
audit.corrected: Rows 4-5 and 6 to Irelia; row 7 (2+ items) to Skill, matching the packet chart, the win rate and the late-game text. Proposed as matched full/content pairs.

audit.why: Spikes are level 3 (E online), level 6 (Vanguard's Edge vs Demonic Ascension), first item, and Swain's late scaling — all four present and correctly ordered. Swain's R is a flat 120s at every rank, so there is no rank-based ult spike to add.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly claims Defiant Dance (W) 'blanks his Q (Death's Hand) cone and W detonation'. Riot's text for Defiant Dance says she takes reduced PHYSICAL damage during the charge; Swain's Q, W and R are magic. It also claims Irelia's passive 'shreds his MR' — the passive grants stacking attack speed and bonus on-hit damage at max stacks, no resistance shred.
audit.why: Two fabricated interactions telling the player to tank a magic-damage combo behind a physical-only mitigation. That gets people killed in the exact window the page tells them to fight.
audit.corrected: State Defiant Dance is physical-only and does not blunt his magic; replace the MR-shred claim with the real passive (stacking attack speed, on-hit bonus at max). Add the two missing-interaction items: Ravenous Flock heals and grows his max HP, so Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades and raw resistance stacking is not the answer. Nevermove roots on the return pass, so dodge the way back; it is down 12s at rank 1 (10s at rank 5, shorter during Demonic Ascension). Death's Hand is on 7s at rank 1 falling to 3s.

audit.why: Executioner's Calling is already named in report[8]; the missing-interaction anti-heal rule is now also carried into the do's and wants where the player will actually read it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page tells the player Nevermove only roots on its return pass.
audit.why: It is the single decisive dodge in the lane and the trigger for every all-in.
audit.corrected: Added to dosFull[2].d and kept consistent with the existing wants.foe[0] framing.

edits.before: Defiant Dance's damage reduction comes online, letting you trade through his Q cone and W detonation in a fight his pre-6 sustain can't win.
edits.after: Defiant Dance cuts physical damage only, so it blanks none of his magic — trade off the wave while Death's Hand sits on its 7s cooldown at rank 1.

edits.before: Your passive stacks and Q cooldowns tighten, so you stay glued through his root and your armor/MR shred out-damages his pre-R healing.
edits.after: Your passive stacks and Q cooldowns tighten, so you stay glued through his root and out-damage his pre-6 healing — Q is down to 7s at rank 4.

edits.before: Trinity Force online is your peak: Bladesurge reset uptime keeps you glued through his slows while Defiant Dance's damage reduction blanks his Q (Death's Hand) cone and his W detonation.
edits.after: Trinity Force online is your peak: Bladesurge reset uptime keeps you glued through his W slow, but Defiant Dance only cuts physical damage — Death's Hand still lands on you in full.

edits.before: This is your window. Sidestep the E return cast, then E-stun in and chain Bladesurge resets off him and the wave — Defiant Dance's damage reduction blanks his Q cone and W detonation while your passive shreds his MR and ramps the longer you stay glued. At 6 his Demonic Ascension wants a long fight, but Vanguard's Edge walls off his retreat so he can't kite the drain away from you. Force the all-in while his E is on cooldown.
edits.after: This is your window. Sidestep the return pass of Nevermove, then E-stun in and chain Bladesurge resets off him and the wave — Defiant Dance cuts physical damage only, so it will not blunt his magic; you win by stacking the passive to max attack speed and never letting him walk away. At 6 his Demonic Ascension wants a long fight, so Grievous Wounds is what beats the drain. Force the all-in while his E is down 12s.

edits.before: Time Defiant Dance to eat his Q (Death's Hand) cone and W detonation during the trade instead of facetanking the whole combo
edits.after: Buy Executioner's Calling early — Grievous Wounds is what stops Ravenous Flock and his R drain out-healing everything you land

edits.before: Charge 4 passive stacks on minions, E-stun Swain when his answer is down, and Q-reset through the wave onto the kill.
edits.after: Mercury's Treads plus Wit's End answer his magic, and Executioner's Calling stops Ravenous Flock topping him back up.

edits.before: Swain wastes Demonic Ascension — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: It roots on the return pass, not the first — dodge back through it.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Rooted, you eat every bolt of Death's Hand and his W on top.

notes: Two fabricated interactions removed: Defiant Dance (W) reduces PHYSICAL damage only per Riot's text and cannot mitigate Swain's all-magic kit, and Irelia's passive grants stacking attack speed / on-hit damage, not armour or MR shred. Both appeared in multiple fields. Level chart: full and content agreed with each other but disagreed with the packet chart on rows 4-7; flipped 4-5 and 6 to Irelia and 7 to Skill as matched pairs so the prose, the win rate (53.54% over 508 games) and the chart all say the same thing. suspectNames flagged 'Defiant Dance's' and 'Keep Demonic Ascension' — both are false positives on names; the real ability names were correct, the mechanics attached to them were not.
